abstract:
The systemic biochemical diversity of circulating metabolites and lipids reflects the integrated effects of genetic variation and environmental exposure. Metabolite quantitative trait locus (mQTL) studies in humans have established gene-metabolite associations, but genetic contributions can be obscured by sex, diet, age, medication use, and environmental exposures. Genetically diverse model systems offer a powerful complementary strategy to isolate genetic contributions to the biochemical diversity of the circulating metabolome.
We applied mass spectrometry profiling to serum samples in 541 mice from the Diversity Outbred (DO) population and identified 1,933 mQTL across 240 metabolites, 561 lipids, 43 oxylipins, and 4,465 MS/MS features. QTL hotspots on chromosomes 8, 9, 10, and 17 implicated distinct loci in the regulation of serum lipids, metabolites, and peptide-like features. The chromosome 8 Ces1 and Ces2 gene clusters were associated with lipids, acylcarnitines, and acyl-CoAs, while chromosome 9 and 10 loci included additional lipid and metabolite QTL. On chromosome 17, MHC and C3 regions were associated with untargeted peptide-like MS/MS features. Comparisons with matched red blood cell mQTL revealed widespread compartment-specific genetic control.
Collectively, these findings provide a high-resolution map of the genetic regulation of the circulating metabolome, offering mechanistic insights that complement and extend human metabolic genetics.
